verdict.root_cause: The evidence does not identify a culprit. All seven dispatches examined cart (plus empty change-log lookups for cart, flagd and product-catalog), and they exonerate cart rather than convict it: cart's errored-span ratio is exactly zero with zero variance across both incident and baseline windows [tr_6530d8ba7410, tr_886f13db48d0], its logs at both window edges are clean informational store operations with the process still serving several requests per second at 23:27:16 [tr_3830cc2c1d5e], and in the sampled traces cart handler self-time, Valkey leaf spans and flagd resolution are all sub-millisecond with no timeout-shaped spans [tr_c306b4a57139]. No deploy, config edit or flag flip was recorded for cart, flagd or product-catalog [tr_8da4d0070c44, tr_c4cbf4267c93, tr_592e96e48285], though those queries ran forward from onset and do not cover the hours before it. The one genuinely anomalous signal is that cart trace data stops at 22:58:29 — roughly 27 minutes before the 23:25:31 alert and continuing to the window edge — while cart's span-metrics denominator stays populated and its logs keep flowing [tr_c306b4a57139, tr_886f13db48d0, tr_3830cc2c1d5e]. That combination is a telemetry/export gap, not a service failure, and no service other than cart was ever examined, so the actual fault among the 14 affected services remains unidentified.
verdict.reasoning: A verdict needs a service whose own signals show the failing mechanism. Cart shows none: zero errors, zero latency elevation, a live process logging normally, and healthy downstream hops [tr_6530d8ba7410, tr_886f13db48d0, tr_3830cc2c1d5e, tr_c306b4a57139]. Cart also cannot be a silent hang (process_freeze) or a partition, because it keeps logging and keeps recording calls through the window edge [tr_3830cc2c1d5e, tr_886f13db48d0]. The change log is empty for the three services queried, removing the usual bad_deploy/bad_config/feature_flag anchors for those three [tr_8da4d0070c44, tr_c4cbf4267c93, tr_592e96e48285], and the windows ran forward from onset so a pre-onset change is unqueried. Checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator all alerted at the same second and none was investigated; errors propagate toward the caller, so the originator is plausibly downstream of cart or elsewhere entirely. Naming a class now would be inference from the absence of dispatches rather than from evidence.
open_questions: Why do cart traces stop at 22:58:29 while its logs and span metrics continue — broken trace export, a sampling change, or genuine loss of sampled requests?
What do checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy show for error ratio, latency and logs at 23:25:31? None of the co-alerting services was dispatched.
Were there any changes in the hours *before* 23:25:31? All three change queries ran forward from onset, leaving the lead-up uncovered.

alternatives.root_cause: A dependency downstream of checkout or frontend became slow and the latency propagated up to the alerting edge services.
alternatives.why_not: Entirely unexamined — no checkout, frontend or frontend-proxy dispatch was run, and the only traces available show sub-20ms end-to-end paths with no slow hop [tr_c306b4a57139].

alternatives.root_cause: Cart's telemetry pipeline, not cart itself, failed — trace export stopped at 22:58:29 and the alert reflects missing data rather than a user-visible fault.
alternatives.why_not: Would not explain why 14 services were affected or why four other services alerted at the same second; it also leaves cart's metrics and logs flowing normally, which a wholesale telemetry failure would not [tr_886f13db48d0, tr_3830cc2c1d5e].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no change in any observable signal is expected. The investigation should continue: the next observations that would change this answer are error-ratio, latency-percentile and log queries on checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy at 23:25:31, and change-history queries run backward from onset rather than forward.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a dispatch on one of the co-alerting services (checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy) or a backward-looking change query surfaces a deploy, config edit or flag flip inside the incident window, or shows a service whose error ratio or latency actually stepped at 23:25:31. Any of those would meet a rollback_image or revert_config precondition and a targeted proposal should then replace this one. It is also wrong if the cart trace gap at 22:58:29 turns out to be in-process exporter state rather than a collector-side problem — but nothing in the current evidence distinguishes those two, and the distinguishing observation (collector/export health) is not on this board at all.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that the fault persists unmitigated while 14 services remain affected and five continue alerting. That is accepted here because every permitted action is scoped to a single service and the faulting service has not been identified; acting on the only service examined would be acting on the one service the evidence exonerates.
proposal.blast_radius: None. No service is touched, no container is recreated, no caller sees a connection reset. The cost is elapsed incident time only.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Five services across the checkout path alerted simultaneously, which is a synchronized multi-service failure rather than a single noisy latency warning. No open incident covers it, and the shared dependencies (cart/checkout/frontend fan-in) give no single obvious culprit yet.
